about: Rules of scripts/kinguin-deals.mjs (it runs every morning and writes data/kinguin.json). feed = which feed of data/feeds.json (kinguin) to read. Stage 1, from the feed only: platforms = only keys for these platforms; regionMustContain = the region text must contain one of these words (case does not matter) and the product must have no country limits; minPrice and maxPrice = Kinguin price in USD; excludeNames = words in a product name that mean it is not a plain game key. Stage 2, Steam price: minSteamPrice = the current Steam price in USD must be at least this; minSavingsPct = the Kinguin key must be at least this % cheaper than the CURRENT Steam price (it already includes any Steam sale); maxSavingsPct = a key MORE than this % cheaper than Steam is not shown: such prices are too good to be reliable (gray-market keys from cheap regions, bundle leftovers or worse; owner decision of 11 Oct 2026, a starting value that can be changed); maxPriceChecks = safety limit for how many games we ask Steam about. Stage 3, quality: games are looked at in order of Steam list price (high first: bigger games are better known), until maxSteamRequests Steam requests are used (answers are remembered for days, so later runs go further); minReviews and minPositive = Steam reviews (same as the main site rules); adultFlags = Steam content flags we never show; minStock = keys in stock. The accepted games are ranked by the number of Steam reviews (best known first) and the first maxOutput are written to data/kinguin.json. The main site decides how many of them it shows (maxNew per day, maxTotal).
